No—if the document matches an existing send, the current export flow rejects it **before calling the provider**.

Two document-level refusals exist:

| Reason | Condition |
|---|---|
| `already_sent` | An existing record has upload status `uploaded`, processing status other than `archived`, and the **same return type**. |
| `upload_in_progress` | An existing record has upload status `waiting` or `uploading`. This check applies **across return types**. |

Both checks are scoped to the same **firm, client, contact, tax year, provider, and document ID**. `already_sent` takes precedence when both match. See [ValidateDocuments](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:89).

Consequences:

- An archived upload does **not** block sending again.
- An uploaded document under another return type does **not** trigger `already_sent`; a pending upload under another return type still blocks it.
- Failed uploads do not trigger either refusal merely because they failed.
- Unsupported return type or tax year is checked first, so that refusal can mask the duplicate/in-flight reason.

Rejected documents are returned as `{document_id, reason, message}`. If **all documents are rejected**, the service returns successfully with an empty accepted list, before creating send records or invoking the provider. In a mixed batch, only accepted documents proceed to provider dispatch. See [ExportAsync#perform](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:66).
